title: How to Deal With Travel Anxiety on a Road Trip: What Helps Me
summary: I live with travel anxiety, so road trips can get tricky. Here are the 4 things that keep me calm on the road, from packing a calm down kit to taking breaks.
body_markdown:
## How I Decrease Travel Anxiety While Road-Tripping


Over the years, I’ve landed on a handful of travel anxiety tips that help me feel calmer between destinations. Here’s what’s in my road trip routine.


1.


#### I Pack a “Calm Down” Kit


I always make sure that I have my[toolkit](https://lifestance.com/blog/anxiety-toolkit/) with me in the car. In a small bag that will fit at my feet, I pack the following: a bottle of[lavender essential oil](https://lifestance.com/blog/aromatherapy-products-for-mood/) , charging cords and my iPad so I can keep myself busy with something distracting, and a Warmie (seriously, if you’re someone who deals with mental health stuff regularly, I can’t say enough about these stuffed animals who can be warmed in the microwave – I warm up my little sloth whenever I can, but otherwise, he’s just a good[comfort item](https://lifestance.com/blog/psychological-benefits-comfort-objects/) ).


2.


#### I Take Naps


Even though it can be tough in the car (since I’m someone who usually needs a just-right environment to sleep), I make sure I snooze periodically so I can keep my anxiety down. To achieve some ZZZs, I pack a small travel blanket, a pillow for behind my neck, and an eye mask so I can keep out the daylight.


3.


#### I Focus on What’s Around Me


Luckily, on the vast majority of our road trips, there’s always something interesting to look at out the window. When I feel anxiety creeping in, I make sure to focus on what’s going on outwardly instead of inwardly – a simple[grounding technique](https://lifestance.com/blog/grounding-techniques-for-anxiety/) that pulls me out of my head. This might mean counting billboards, looking at pretty, nature-filled scenery, and keeping my eye out for cool, vintage cars.


4.


#### I Take Breaks


On a day-to-day basis, I’m a big fan of taking breaks. I regularly need to reset my brain, and it’s no different while road-tripping. Every hour or two, my husband and I make sure to stop and stretch our legs. We prioritize unique rest stops (with natural overlooks or mini museums) and stop midday for a picnic lunch, too. I’ve even been known to jog a bit as relief from the long car ride. Breaks are good in general as we go through life, and they tend to be even better if you’re on the road and your destination is miles and miles away.


None of these habits make my travel anxiety vanish completely, but together they keep it manageable enough that I can keep saying yes to the next road trip.
